gap: No result ChatGPT got states that CKL's $149.99 622DP-4, the budget card in both chats, has no EDID emulation, even though both answers list EDID emulation as a priority. CKL's own store says "This DisplayPort KVM switch does not support EDID emulation so the desktop locations may change upon switching and boot-up." CKL's model with EDID emulation is the 622DP-5 at $379.00, more than the $329.90 TESmart DKS202-M24 that does have it.
standout_why: Compared against the cited TESmart DKS202-M24 page and three of the top results: dockgearhq.com (2026-09-12), tradingdeskgear.com (2026-11-06) and gearexplained.com/guides/dual-monitor-kvm-switch (2026-10-05). I also checked streamingjet.com. The rivals already give the EDID verdict for TESmart (has it) and Level1Techs (no monitor emulation). Tradingdeskgear also has Level1Techs at 4K 120 Hz and ties TESmart's 144 Hz to DSC. None of them mentions any CKL model, so nobody checks the budget pick against the EDID priority. None says either that DP 1.4 cannot carry 4K 144 Hz without DSC or 4:2:2. Every "4K 144Hz" rating (TESmart, CKL, StarTech) therefore depends on DSC or 4:2:2, while Level1Techs' "4K/120" is the figure without either. Dockgearhq ties DSC only to TESmart's 8K60 mode, and tradingdeskgear ties it only to TESmart's 144 Hz figure.
decides: It confirms TESmart DKS202-M24 ($329.90 on tesmart.com, 2026-11-13) as the pick for a shopper who wants EDID emulation and 4K 144 Hz. It takes away the $149.99 CKL 622DP-4's case as the budget option for anyone who listed EDID as a priority: the cheaper CKL with emulation (622DP-5) costs $379.00, more than the TESmart. The 622DP-4 is still a sound $150 option if windows rearranging on each switch is acceptable. The normalised refresh column also ranks Level1Techs ($520+, 4K 120 Hz, no monitor emulation) below the TESmart for this question unless the shopper has keyboards that cause trouble with other KVMs.
